definition: Excavate means to dig out of the ground and remove.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word excavate. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know excavate should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Badgers had excavated a den under the shed, throwing out a fan of sandy soil overnight.
Scoop is the smallest gesture, nowhere near excavate — a trowel of loose soil lifted in a second, nothing like the methodical, large-scale digging and removal that excavating names.
Dig is stronger than scoop but plainer than excavate: anyone can dig a hole, while excavating means digging material out and removing it, methodically and at scale.

To unearth is to dig something up and bring it to light — the spotlight is on the find, the coin or fossil suddenly in your hand. Excavate spotlights the labor instead: methodical digging on a serious scale, with the spoil removed and carried away. You unearth a treasure; you excavate the site around it.

To exhume is to dig up from a grave, specifically — the word English reserves for undoing a burial, usually a body and usually under legal order. Excavate is the general working word for digging material out and removing it at scale: pits, foundations, whole buried cities.

The hillside above Ruby Creek looked unremarkable until a rancher's dog began worrying at what turned out to be a rib the size of a fence post.
By midsummer a crew of twelve was working to excavate the slope: they cut a terrace into the hill, gridded it with string, and began taking the rock down in numbered blocks.
Nothing about the work was quick.
Each block was logged, wrapped in plaster, and winched onto a flatbed; by September the crew had removed sixty tons of stone.
The skeleton itself — a long-necked giant, two-thirds complete — stayed encased until the lab could open the jackets under proper light.
'People imagine the moment of discovery,' the lead paleontologist said.
'Mostly what we do is move a hillside, carefully, one block at a time.'
